records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — [P2, confidence 75, advisory] With two external issues from the same integration linked to one Sentry group, `if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id:` suppresses propagation to the second issue when the first changes assignee, leaving that customer’s linked issues inconsistent; the strongest rebuttal is that integration-wide suppression intentionally prevents echoes, but the second issue is a distinct destination already supported by the outbound GroupLink fanout, so preserving the originating external issue key and excluding only that issue prevents the echo without deleting valid synchronization edges.
records.rationale: The finding describes a scenario where two different Sentry groups are linked to the same integration. Looking at the diff, the `should_sync` method at line 390 checks `if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id: return False`. This means when an inbound assignment comes from integration X, it will block ALL outbound syncs to integration X, regardless of which external issue triggered the inbound sync.
